Skokie, IL · Chicago area

I help small businesses automate.

If you want to automate your manual workflows and don't know how to start — you're in the right place.





How it works

1. We talk. We get on Zoom and you tell me how your business really runs. One conversation about your actual week. You don’t need a plan or any tech knowledge.

2. I map it. We find where your time and money are going, and pick the best first piece to automate.

3. I build it. With AI build tools, what used to take months now takes days or weeks. Your first piece is built around how your business already works.

4. You try it. Use it in your real work. Send me one round of changes, and I’ll make them and send it back.

5. You own it. If you like it, pay for it in full and it’s yours. I stay with you after it goes live.

6. We do it again. When the first piece is paying for itself, we pick the next one and build that. One piece at a time.

Hello, and welcome.

Examples of work

Site diagrams drawn on the job
The estimator draws the basement or foundation on a tablet, dropping in beams, piers, sump pumps, drains and window wells, with measurements and a legend that builds itself. The sketch done on site is the finished drawing. Nobody redraws it back at the office, and the customer sees it in their quote.

AI that makes art in my style
A customer picks a photo from their camera roll. The system turns it into a piece in my style, trained on my own work. My style becomes something people can buy without me hand-making each piece.

A website in three languages
Every page reads in English, Spanish or Portuguese, switched from the top of the page. The lab works across the US, the UK and Brazil. Everyone reads it in their own language.

Warranties that send themselves
When an invoice is paid in full, the system works out which warranties the job earned, makes the certificates and a paid-in-full receipt, and emails them to the customer. Customers get their paperwork the same day, and nobody in the office has to remember to send it.

Your art on a shirt that turns
The customer's art goes straight onto a shirt that rotates on screen. They can see it from every side before they buy. People buy with confidence when they see exactly what they're getting.

Sign-ups and reminders for the writing group
Members join the monthly writing group from the website. Before each session they get an email reminder with a calendar invite. The group runs itself. No one keeps a list or sends reminder emails by hand.

Crew schedule
A month and week calendar of every job. Moving a job is one drag, and multi-day jobs, deadlines and crew notes sit right on it. It replaces the whiteboard and the phone calls. The crew can see their day.

A members-only library
A protected library of teaching material. Members get in with a key the lab controls, and changing the key signs everyone out at once. Sensitive research stays private, and the lab decides who sees it.

Card payments on every invoice
Each invoice has a pay-by-card link the office can text or email. Card payments, deposits and checks are all recorded against it, and it shows what is still owed. Customers can pay the day the work is done, and the office knows who owes what without a spreadsheet.

A store off Shopify
The full catalog, 84 products across shirts, hoodies and prints, moved to a store we own, with card checkout. No Shopify subscription, and the shop looks and works exactly the way we want.

The owner's morning view
One screen shows bids waiting for approval, today's jobs and the whole bid pipeline in dollars. The owner sees what needs attention first thing, without asking anyone.

A speakers directory
A page of scholars and artists who can visit a class, with their topics, languages and whether they come virtually or in person. New speakers apply from the same page. Teachers can find the right voice for their course in minutes.

Contracts signed on the customer's phone
The customer gets a link to their contract, reviews the work and the price, and signs with a finger. No printing, scanning or driving out for a signature.

Booking a speaker
Teachers fill in their course, topic, format and dates, and the request goes straight to the lab. Every request is in one place, with what's needed to make the match.

811 calls tracked before every dig
The system lists every signed job that needs an 811 call, works out when the marks will be ready and how long they last, and flags any job that hasn't been called yet. No crew shows up to dig before the lines are marked.

A site the lab runs itself
Graduate students update the podcast, projects and news from a simple admin page. When they save, the other two languages are translated automatically. The lab keeps its site current without waiting on a developer.

A weekly supply order that writes itself
From past purchases and the jobs on the schedule, the system builds this week's order: what to buy, how many, and how sure it is about each number. The order is ready every week, based on what the business actually uses.

Have a hunch?

Have a hunch something in your business could run on its own? You don't need to know what to call it. Tell me how your day goes, and we'll figure it out together.
